clue.text: Detective is trailing money once spent abroad by author

indicators.note: trailing means the word is comes behind the coin, following it in the answer

parts.note: dick is old slang for a detective
the franc was the currency of France before the euro
taken as written

explanation.surface: A private eye follows old foreign currency left behind by a writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Detective' wants to be the definition, but it is the first piece; the author is the jockey-turned-thriller writer, and 'trailing' sets the short word behind the old French coin.
explanation.definitionFit: The jockey-turned-novelist wrote racing thrillers, so he is a well-known example of an author.

clue.text: Poor dolt in Paris found out what the lion's share is

indicators.note: found out suggests the letters have been sorted and worked out afresh, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A clumsy Parisian fool works out how big the lion's portion is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found out' rearranges all fifteen letters of POOR DOLT IN PARIS.
explanation.definitionFit: The lion's share is the largest portion, far more than an equal split, hence out of balance.

clue.text: See 7
Place for water in a cheese

parts.note: a font is the basin holding holy water in a church
taken as written

explanation.surface: A church basin sits inside a cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a container signal but is simply its own two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Fontina is a soft Italian cow's-milk variety from the Aosta valley.

clue.text: Angry gathering introduces science to a good queen

indicators.note: introduces ... to means the science abbreviation is brought inside the queen's name

parts.note: Good Queen Bess was the nickname of Elizabeth I
Sc is the standard abbreviation for science

explanation.surface: A furious crowd brings learning to a kindly monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: Good Queen Bess was Elizabeth I's nickname. 'introduces' (with 'to') places the science abbreviation inside her name. 'Angry gathering' sounds like a mob, but it is medical: an inflamed swelling.
explanation.definitionFit: An abscess is an inflamed, swollen collection of pus, which is an angry gathering in medical terms.

clue.text: Craze on what it might be to be crazy

indicators.note: in a down clue on means placed above, so the first word goes before the second

parts.note: crazing is fine cracking in a glaze, so a craze is a crack
a craze in glaze might well be on a piece of pottery

explanation.surface: A fad catches on, and anyone joining it must be mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Craze' means the fine cracks in glazed pottery, not a fad. 'on' puts CRACK above POT.
explanation.definitionFit: A crackpot idea or person is eccentric and unhinged, so the word serves as a synonym for crazy.

clue.text: Try it on partners who take trouble to soil their opponents in Germany

indicators.note: who take means the partner letters hold the trouble between them

parts.note: in bridge South and North play as partners
to ail is to trouble or afflict
earth means soil
East and West oppose North and South at bridge
taken as written
D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: A bridge pair goes to great lengths to dirty the opposition in Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: Bridge seats are North, South, East and West: North-South partner each other against East-West. 'who take' puts the trouble inside the partners' letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Sailing close to the wind means risking breaking the rules, as does trying it on, an idiom for testing limits.

clue.text: Bits of a play that's 14: 12, 24 … and 15?

definitions.meaning: the devotional sequence of fourteen scenes from the Passion, a play with the 14-across opening
the entries numbered 12, 24 and 15 each pair with the second half of this answer to name London stations or a medal

explanation.surface: A theatre-goer cross-references scenes of a play with other answers in the grid.
explanation.walkthrough: KING'S Cross and CHARING Cross are London railway stations; VICTORIA is one too, but the question mark covers the Victoria Cross, the gallantry medal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Stations are fourteen episodes of Christ's last day, often staged in Passion plays.

clue.text: Is dye pleasing in this arrangement?

definitions.text: Is dye pleasing in this arrangement?

indicators.note: arrangement asks for the preceding letters to be put in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a colour looks good laid out in a particular way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in this arrangement' rearranges IS DYE PLEASING; the whole clue also asks about a dyed fabric pattern.
explanation.definitionFit: The teardrop motif is a dyed fabric pattern, so the clue's question about a pleasing dyed arrangement describes it.

clue.text: Relates to one's source of cash in the past

definitions.text: source of cash in the past

indicators.note: the 's stands for has: the words relates to one have the answer within them

explanation.surface: Someone recounts where their money once came from.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's in one's reads as 'has', telling you the answer is inside RELATES TO ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: A testoon was an old silver coin of Tudor England and Renaissance Europe, so it was once a source of cash.

clue.text: Power to keep going in adversity excites when lacking energy

indicators.note: adverse literally means turned against, so the word is turned backwards
when lacking means the energy letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: to animate is to excite or enliven
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Endurance in hard times stirs people who have run out of puff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when lacking' drops E from ANIMATES to give ANIMATS, which 'in adversity' turns backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Stamina is staying power, the physical capacity to keep going under strain.

clue.text: Spinner allowing one run lets it slip

indicators.note: to slip is to slide out of place, so the letters move into a new order

explanation.surface: A bowler allows a single and then lets the ball get away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slip' rearranges RUN and LETS IT. The cricket picture of a spin bowler conceding a run misleads.
explanation.definitionFit: A turnstile is a revolving gate admitting people one at a time, a spinner allowing a single person through.

clue.text: Where to learn the three R's?

definitions.meaning: ... College in Cambridge or London is a seat of learning
R stands for rex, Latin for a male monarch, so three Rs are three royal rulers

explanation.walkthrough: The 'three R's' are usually reading, writing and arithmetic; here each R is Rex.
explanation.definitionFit: King's is a famous college, and R is the abbreviation for a monarch, so three of them are crowned rulers.

clue.text: Cry over spilt milk?

parts.note: not weeping in regret, as the proverb suggests, but the exclamation someone makes at the moment of spilling

explanation.definitionFit: It is the little exclamation people blurt out when they make a clumsy mistake like knocking over a glass.

clue.text: Size keeps Society Island hot

indicators.note: keeps means holds inside, so the paste word contains the others

parts.note: size is a gluey paste used to stiffen paper or prepare walls
Iona is a Scottish island in the Inner Hebrides

explanation.surface: Glue holds a Pacific archipelago in the heat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Society Island' suggests the Pacific group, but it splits into an abbreviation and a Hebridean island, which 'keeps' places inside the glue.
explanation.definitionFit: Passionate means ardent or fervent, and hot is used in the same sense of strong feeling or desire.

clue.text: Reported as plumb line falls?

definitions.meaning: said like plumb, that is, plum: a popular English plum variety
a London Underground line of the same name
the great waterfall on the Zambezi between Zambia and Zimbabwe

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a builder's plumb line dropping; read instead plum (said like plumb), Line and Falls, each preceded by the same queen's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The queen's name precedes a plum variety, a Tube line in London and the great falls on the Zambezi.

clue.text: Racism even affected one in the wars

indicators.note: affected means altered or influenced, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Prejudice still touched a soldier fighting abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'affected' rearranges RACISM EVEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A serviceman is a member of the armed forces, someone who fights in the wars.

clue.text: Digitised fish need to be swimming around

indicators.note: around means the rearranged letters surround the fish
swimming suggests the letters move about freely, so they are rearranged

parts.note: the cod is a common food fish

explanation.surface: Computerised fish have to swim about in circles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be swimming' scrambles the four letters of need, and 'around' wraps them round the fish; the surface's swimming fish is a decoy.
explanation.definitionFit: Data that is digitised has been converted into code, a computing sense of encoded.

clue.text: Could be an item

definitions.meaning: the little word an belongs to a grammatical class, the indefinite kind used before nouns
an item in a newspaper or list is a piece or entry

explanation.definitionFit: In grammar 'an' is the indefinite type of this part of speech, and the word also means a single item or piece.

clue.text: Horse's upright member

definitions.meaning: read as horse is: a stallion kept for breeding
in carpentry a vertical post in a timber wall frame

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a stallion kept for breeding and a vertical timber in a wall frame.

clue.text: Off-load gold in the Bronx?

indicators.note: the question mark asks how the word would be spoken in a New York accent

parts.note: gold is the medal for first place

explanation.surface: A New Yorker dumps a stash of precious metal.
explanation.walkthrough: In a stereotypical Brooklyn or Bronx accent 'first' is said 'foist'; gold medals go to whoever finishes first.
explanation.definitionFit: To foist something on someone is to off-load an unwanted thing onto them.

clue.text: Its stance displayed the heart of a lion

indicators.note: displayed suggests the letters are laid out anew in a different order

explanation.surface: A big cat's posture showed true courage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'displayed' rearranges ITS STANCE. 'the heart of a lion' suggests courage, but means a lion's feline nature.
explanation.definitionFit: A lion is a big cat, so its essential nature is catlike, a whimsical sense of spite's synonym.

clue.text: As potato growers might have said here in America?

definitions.text: As potato growers might have said here in America?

parts.words: As potato growers might have said here in America?
parts.note: picture a farmer saying they owned a garden tool for earthing up potatoes, in words that run together into the name of a potato-growing US state

explanation.definitionFit: The north-western US state is renowned for its potato crop, and its name sounds like a farmer saying they owned a hoe.

clue.text: Number used more than once in division

definitions.text: used more than once in division
definitions.meaning: an old subdivision of an English county, several of which made up a shire

explanation.definitionFit: It is both the figure ten times ten and an old administrative subdivision of an English shire.

clue.text: Doing series about King George I

indicators.note: about means the series word goes round the royal letter

parts.note: a chain is a connected series
R stands for rex, Latin for king

indicators.note: I read as the Roman numeral one, the first letter of the name

explanation.surface: A run of events concerning the first Hanoverian monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'George I' looks like the Hanoverian king; read it as George's first letter. 'about' puts R inside CHAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: To char is to do housework for pay, so charing means doing the cleaning, as in doing for someone.

clue.text: This'll surprise you in advance: Nelson's after honoured lady

indicators.note: after means the wrestling word comes behind the honour

parts.note: an advance of money is a loan
DBE, Dame Commander of the Order of the British Empire, is an honour for women
a nelson is a wrestling hold, the 's read as is

explanation.surface: An admiral follows a decorated woman ahead of everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: Nelson suggests the admiral, but a (full) nelson is a wrestling hold; DBE is the female knighthood equivalent.
explanation.definitionFit: The old exclamation calls attention to something astonishing, so it is said when something will surprise you.
